clue.text: Think about bitterness recalled in court

indicators.note: 'in' places the reversed words inside the word for court

parts.note: to court someone is to date them

indicators.note: to recall is to call back, so the letters run back the way they came

parts.note: bile is a byword for bitterness or ill temper
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A judge pondering the bitter feelings that resurfaced during a trial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'court' looks like a law court, but it is the verb meaning to woo; 'about' joins the bitterness word before both are turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: To deliberate is to consider carefully, a fuller synonym for think as a verb.

clue.text: Ruin career

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to wreck, as hopes are wrecked

explanation.walkthrough: 'career' reads as a noun, a working life, but here it is the verb meaning to hurtle along.
explanation.definitionFit: One short verb covers both destroying hopes and rushing at speed, two unrelated senses.

clue.text: Meeting area is claimed by Pride participant

indicators.note: something claimed by another is taken into its possession, so it ends up held inside

parts.note: a pride is a group of lions, so a member is a lion
A is the abbreviation for area
taken as written

explanation.surface: A designated zone for gatherings has been taken over by a marcher at a Pride parade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pride' suggests a parade, but it is the collective noun for lions.
explanation.definitionFit: A liaison is a meeting or contact, especially a secret or romantic one.

clue.text: Tough start for temp if bias gets involved

indicators.note: letters that get involved are tangled together and come out in a new order

parts.note: all thirteen letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A temporary worker finds the first days hard because of prejudice in the office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' looks like a link word but its letters are part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A baptism of fire is an idiom for a difficult first experience in a new role.

clue.text: Crowds promoting River Island

indicators.note: to promote is to move up, and in a down light that means bringing a letter to the top

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for river
hordes are large crowds

explanation.surface: Throngs of shoppers advertising a high-street clothing chain called River Island.
explanation.walkthrough: River Island is a British fashion retailer, which makes the two words look like one name. The river letter already in the crowds word moves up to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhodes is a Greek island in the Dodecanese, a specific example of an island.

clue.text: Straight talker upset himself until going to extremes

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its two ends, so only first and last letters of each word are kept

parts.note: first and last letters
first and last letters
first and last letters
first and last letters

explanation.surface: A blunt speaker gets worked up and goes over the top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Straight talker' reads as one phrase, but only 'Straight' is the definition; 'upset' looks like an indicator and is just fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Straight in the sense of honest and candid is a synonym for truthful.

clue.text: Old city originally didn't use language

parts.note: Ur is the ancient Mesopotamian city, a crossword favourite

indicators.note: originally points to how each word begins, so only the opening letters are kept

parts.note: first letters of the two words

explanation.surface: An ancient city that, from the start, refused to adopt a certain tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: Urdu is the national language of Pakistan, also widely spoken in India.

clue.text: Pause Sixth Sense, breaking tradition

indicators.note: something breaking another splits it open and sits in the gap

parts.note: a rite is a traditional ceremony or custom
extrasensory perception, often called the sixth sense

explanation.surface: A viewer stops the film The Sixth Sense, departing from the family's usual movie-night routine.
explanation.definitionFit: A respite is a short break or interval of relief, so a pause.

clue.text: Briefs about German delinquent not taken in

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the underwear word goes round the next letter

parts.note: briefs are underpants, informally undies
G is the abbreviation for German
a Ted, short for Teddy boy, was a 1950s British youth with a delinquent reputation

explanation.surface: Legal briefs concerning a German offender that nobody absorbed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Briefs' suggests legal documents but is underwear here.
explanation.definitionFit: Undigested food has not been absorbed, and figuratively undigested facts have not been understood.

clue.text: Get to hold a fairly soft bathroom cleaner

indicators.note: holding something means keeping it inside, so the dismissal word encloses the rest

parts.note: 'Get!' and 'Shoo!' both order someone away
taken as written
mp, mezzo piano, is the musical marking for moderately soft

explanation.surface: Buy a mild household cleaning product for the bathroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get' reads as obtain, but here it is a command to go away.
explanation.definitionFit: Shampoo is used in the bathroom to clean hair, so a playful description of a cleaner.

clue.text: Natural fluctuation of pound stopped by sale — insiders missed out

indicators.note: something stopped by another is plugged with it, so the other goes inside
a fluctuation is an unsteady shifting, so these letters move around

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the inside letters are left out, so only the two ends survive

parts.note: first and last letters

explanation.surface: A financial commentator calls the pound's ups and downs halted by a sale natural, with insider traders excluded.
explanation.walkthrough: Financial words like 'pound', 'sale' and 'insiders' paint a market report, but each is fodder or an indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: An unposed photograph is natural and spontaneous rather than arranged.

clue.text: Copper rod to extend, twice taking in charge

indicators.note: each of the two words takes the same item inside it, so the insertion happens two times

parts.note: a pole is a long rod
IC is short for in charge; it goes into the rod word
to extend an invitation is to offer it
the same abbreviation used again, as 'twice' says, inside the second word

explanation.surface: Instructions for making a copper rod longer by heating it twice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in charge' gives IC, which goes inside both words. Copper is everyday British slang for a police officer.
explanation.definitionFit: Copper is informal British slang for a member of the police.

clue.text: Relaxing with part of book that's scary

parts.note: the spine is the bound edge of a book
chilling is slang for relaxing

explanation.surface: Unwinding with a book that turns out to be a horror story.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue gives the second half first; 'with' simply puts the two pieces together.
explanation.definitionFit: Something spine-chilling makes a shiver run down the back, so it is frightening.

clue.text: Feature of ground coffee primarily served in raw meals

indicators.note: served in places the letter inside the next word, as food is served in a dish

parts.note: raw skin is sore

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so just the opening letter is kept

parts.note: first letter
board is meals provided, as in bed and board

explanation.surface: Finely ground coffee is the key element of meals of uncooked food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' looks like milled coffee, but it means a sports ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A scoreboard is a fixture at a sports stadium displaying the score.

clue.text: Pictures of submariner clipped and framed by US agency

indicators.note: something framed by another is surrounded by it on all sides

parts.note: the Central Intelligence Agency

indicators.note: clipping trims a bit off the end, so the final letter goes

parts.note: Captain Nemo commands the submarine Nautilus in Jules Verne's novel

explanation.surface: Photographs of a sailor with a short haircut, set up by American spies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'framed' plays on both picture frames and being set up.
explanation.definitionFit: The pictures is an old informal term for the cinema.

clue.text: Save pop singer's look

parts.note: save and but both mean except
Cher is the pop singer, plus the possessive S

explanation.surface: Apart from a pop star's appearance.
explanation.walkthrough: Butcher's is Cockney rhyming slang: butcher's hook rhymes with look.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a butcher's means taking a look, from British rhyming slang.

clue.text: Sad to lose third card game around ambassador's palace

indicators.note: around means encircling, so the game word wraps the next piece
losing the third means the letter in third position is dropped

parts.note: blue means sad
Nim is a game of taking items from piles, played with cards in the film Last Year at Marienbad
HE, His Excellency, is the title of an ambassador

explanation.surface: A dismal envoy loses a third hand of cards around the embassy.
explanation.walkthrough: Blenheim Palace in Oxfordshire is the birthplace of Winston Churchill.
explanation.definitionFit: Blenheim Palace is the stately home of the Dukes of Marlborough, a specific named palace.

clue.text: Component of camera infallibly drops

indicators.note: a component is a part inside the whole, so the answer is a piece of the following words

parts.note: letters running across the two words

explanation.surface: A part of the camera always falls off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drops' looks like a verb but is the plural noun for falling water.
explanation.definitionFit: Rainfall is precipitation, made up of drops of rain.

clue.text: Badly sullied?

indicators.note: badly means done wrongly, so these letters are put together wrongly

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: something badly sullied has been mistreated.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill-used means treated badly or abused, matching being badly dirtied.

clue.text: Old King claiming winning item

indicators.note: claiming something means taking hold of it, so the king's name encloses the next piece

parts.note: Old King Cole of the nursery rhyme
up means ahead, winning

explanation.surface: An old monarch lays claim to a prize-winning object.
explanation.walkthrough: 'item' means a romantic pair, as in 'they are an item', not an object.
explanation.definitionFit: Two people who are an item are a romantic couple.

clue.text: Forego publicity that comes with European grant

parts.note: PR is public relations
E is the abbreviation for European
to cede is to grant or give up

explanation.surface: Turn down publicity that comes attached to a European funding award.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forego' reads as do without, but split as fore-go it means go before.
explanation.definitionFit: To forego in the sense of go before is to precede.

clue.text: Country clubs with an unfulfilled gardener

indicators.note: unfulfilled means not completed, so the word is left without its end

parts.note: C is the card abbreviation for clubs
taken as written
Adam was the first gardener, in Eden

explanation.surface: A rural golf club with a gardener who is dissatisfied.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country clubs' reads as one phrase, but 'Country' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Canada is a country in North America.

clue.text: Sweet option in bagel, cooking with gas

indicators.note: cooking transforms ingredients, so these letters are mixed into something new

parts.note: taken as written
to gas is to talk at length, to waffle

explanation.surface: A dessert choice baked in a bagel on a gas cooker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gas' looks like the cooking fuel, but it is idle talk.
explanation.definitionFit: A Belgian waffle is a thick sweet batter cake, a dessert choice.

clue.text: Immediately cut short, say

indicators.note: cutting short trims the end, so the final letter is lost

parts.note: to say is to state

explanation.surface: An order to stop talking at once.
explanation.walkthrough: Stat is medical jargon from the Latin statim.
explanation.definitionFit: Stat is hospital shorthand meaning at once, without delay.

clue.text: Plain Jane who wrote abridged study of scripture

indicators.note: an abridged work is shortened, so the last letter is cut

parts.note: Jane Austen, the novelist
RE is Religious Education, the school subject

explanation.surface: An unremarkable woman wrote a short Bible study.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plain Jane' reads as one phrase, but 'Plain' is the definition and 'Jane' starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Austere means severely simple and unadorned, a synonym of plain.

clue.text: African party that is not emptying early

parts.note: the African National Congress
i.e. stands for that is

indicators.note: emptying a word removes its insides, leaving just the outside letters

parts.note: first and last letters

explanation.surface: A political party in Africa that is not winding down too soon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'early' looks adverbial, but here it means belonging to remote times.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancient describes very old times, as in early history.

clue.text: Imitate party animal once

parts.note: to do someone is to impersonate them
a do is a party

explanation.surface: Copy a party animal of the past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'party animal' is a ready phrase, but 'animal once' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The dodo is an extinct flightless bird, an animal that existed only in the past.

clue.text: Two people needing time after one is hurt

parts.note: I'm is the contraction of I am, one is
a pair is two
men are people
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Two people need time to recover after one gets injured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two people' reads as a couple, but splits into two separate pieces; 'after' places the 'one is' piece first.
explanation.definitionFit: Hurt as a noun means damage, which is what an impairment is.
